clue.text: Work at school on ballet about Queen's supreme importance

parts.note: prep is homework done by pupils at school
taken as written

indicators.note: the dance word goes about, i.e. around, the royal letters

parts.note: ballet is a kind of dance
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A pupil's homework concerns a ballet about a queen, which is of the greatest importance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ballet' looks like the definition's partner, but it is just a dance form; 'about' wraps it round the Queen's letters. Prep is British school homework.
explanation.definitionFit: Preponderance is dominance or the greater weight of influence, so it means supreme importance.

clue.text: Fury about new diversity

indicators.note: the anger word wraps about, i.e. around, the single letter

parts.note: fury is rage

explanation.surface: Someone is angry about a newly introduced variety.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a variety or spread of different kinds, which is diversity.

clue.text: Gift posted again under pressure

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
something posted again is re-sent

explanation.surface: A gift has been sent a second time under some duress.
explanation.definitionFit: A present is something given, a synonym of gift.

clue.text: Brazil perhaps has old king beheaded

parts.note: Cnut, or Canute, was an eleventh-century king of England

explanation.surface: Someone from Brazil has an ancient monarch executed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brazil' looks like the country but it is the Brazil nut.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazil is an example of a large edible kernel in a hard shell.

clue.text: Put in bar with English? Terminal

parts.note: to elect someone is to put them in office by vote
a rod is a bar

explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a conductor through which current enters or leaves, i.e. a terminal of a cell.

clue.text: Month working in protective garment

a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A month spent working in protective clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is worn over clothes to shield them from dirt, so it is a protective garment.

clue.text: Is youngster allowed in works restaurant?

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a question, 'Is youngster allowed' is 'can teen?'.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a dining hall provided at a factory or office for its staff.

clue.text: Consume as a joke, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is said aloud and the answer sounds like it

parts.note: doing something as a joke is doing it in jest

explanation.surface: Someone eats something just for a laugh, or so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food or drink into the body, i.e. to consume it.

clue.text: Go wrong with delivery run

parts.note: to err is to go wrong
and means together with

explanation.surface: A delivery trip goes off course.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short trip to deliver or collect something, a delivery run.

clue.text: Charge when admitting first of tourists for outdoor event

explanation.definitionFit: A fete is a public open-air celebration with stalls and games, an outdoor event.

clue.text: One no trump concluded as planned

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.definitionFit: Intended describes what was meant or designed, so it matches as planned.

clue.text: Begin with soldier brought up in home country

clue.text: Sacred emblem louts destroyed

clue.text: Bolster failing target for fishermen?

clue.text: Head of old Oxford debating society abandoning university

parts.note: the Oxford Union is the university's famous debating society

clue.text: Villa lick City with no wingers? Criminal

clue.text: Aver bias, terribly harsh

clue.text: Greek character in theatrical Phaedra

explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet, a Greek character.

clue.text: Stringed instrument in sack, we hear

clue.text: Beginning to try a new turn in dance
